purpose: Test whether sequential conditional-risk assay ordering can expose a predeclared developability liability using fewer assays than strong static and threshold-only baselines.

claim_boundary.allowed: On the Jain 2017 complete 10-assay panel, a frozen continuous-value conditional-risk selector shows a retrospective leave-one-antibody-out efficiency and false-reassurance advantage. This is hypothesis-generating only until an independent antibody panel is evaluated.
forbidden: claim that a Jain threshold is clinically dispositive
claim of dollar-cost savings because Jain does not provide assay costs
retuning model form, features, regularization, thresholds, tie breaks, or baselines on Jain after this freeze

source_binding.dataset: Jain et al. 2017 PNAS supplementary biophysical matrix

liability_definition: A declared liability is a crossing of the already-frozen Jain 2017 Table-1 warning threshold for that assay. It is not a clinical-failure label.
cost_definition: Each assay costs one unit because the Jain source does not contain assay-specific dollar or time costs.

evaluation.holdout_rule: For each of the 137 antibodies, all prevalence, coverage, scaling statistics, and logistic model fits exclude the held-out antibody.
evaluation.efficiency_primary: mean number of assays spent before the first declared liability, calculated only among antibodies that have at least one declared liability in the full 10-assay panel
evaluation.safety_primary: false reassurance after budget b: among antibodies with no liability revealed by the selector in the first b assays, the fraction that actually contains at least one declared liability in an unrevealed assay

selector.name: continuous_value_conditional_risk
selector.first_step: Choose the remaining assay with highest leave-one-out training liability prevalence.
selector.later_steps: For every remaining assay, fit a separate regularized logistic model predicting that assay's liability from the continuous values of all assays already observed for the held-out antibody; choose the assay with highest predicted liability probability.
selector.stop_rule: Stop efficiency counting at the first revealed liability. If none is found, all 10 assays are spent.
selector.features: Raw continuous values of previously observed assays; StandardScaler is fitted on the 136 training antibodies at every step before logistic fitting.

baselines.fixed_prevalence: For each holdout, order assays by liability prevalence in the other 136 antibodies, descending; assay name ascending breaks ties.
baselines.greedy_fixed_coverage: For each holdout, build one fixed order by repeatedly choosing the assay that newly covers the most training antibodies not already covered by an earlier assay; assay name ascending breaks ties.
baselines.uniform_random_expected: Analytic expected first-liability position under a uniformly random assay permutation; no Monte Carlo seed or luck is used.
baselines.binary_dynamic: Same sequential LogisticRegression and scaling/tie rules as the selector, but previously observed assay inputs are encoded only as threshold-clean/threshold-liability 0/1 values rather than continuous measurements.

required_panel_properties: independent antibody measurements with at least three overlapping or prospectively mapped developability assays
thresholds frozen before selector scoring on that panel
enough complete or protocol-admissible candidates to contain both liability-positive and liability-negative cases
required_controls: a separately preregistered standard information-gain or expected-information-gain baseline
external_confirmation_rule.interpretation: If the frozen continuous selector does not retain an efficiency advantage without worsening false reassurance against the strongest admissible control, the cross-panel allocation claim is not supported.
